newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS-DAY EIGHT SNIPPETS AT WIMBLEDON.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-DAY EIGHT SNIPPETS AT WIMBLEDON.

text.p: Day eight snippets from Wimbledon on Monday:

Quote of the day - "They try their best but the difference between playing Wimbledon and an Indian satellite tournament...it's just like going to the moon." Britain's Mark Petchey reflects on his varied career.

Stat of the day - 3. The combined number of U.S. representatives left in the last 16 of the men's and women's singles at Wimbledon. Pete Sampras, Richey Reneberg and Mary Joe Fernandez are the only survivors past the third round.
Grass master - Boris Becker has won more matches on grass than any other active player. His third round win over Britain's Mark Petchey boosted his career record on the surface to 111-21.
Betting nerves - The progress of Tim Henman and Greg Rusedski at Wimbledon has worried only one group of Brits, the betting industry.

Bookmakers William Hill stand to lose one million pounds ($1.7 million) if either of Britain's top two should triumph in the final. Rusedski, a 33-1 shot before the tournament, has moved to 8-1 fourth favourite, while 14th seed Henman is now seventh favourite at 16-1.
Two years ago, the company offered 1000-1 against a British Wimbledon winner.
Fast women - Brenda Schultz-McCarthy has broken her old record for the fastest serve by a woman. The Dutch player clocked 197.9 kph (123 mph) in her second round match against Amy Frazier.
